text_fidelity_a: Holy Stone HS340 Mini FPV Drones with Camera for Kids 8-12 RC Quadcopter for Adults Beginners with One Key Take Off/Landing, Gravity Sensor, Headless Mode, Waypoint Fly, Throw to Go, Indoor & Outdoor I purchased this mini drone because I purchased a HD175D and wanted to learn how to use a drone before trying a more expensive one. So I read the instructions and got the HS340 working  (hoovering) without too much hassle. I tried using the cell phone and camera portion but that would not work so I just settled with the remote control by itself. This worked fine so I began trying to learn to steer I kept it very basic, no tricks or anything that a kid might want to try indoors. After about 5 minutes of getting used to this tiny drone it hit the wall (4 feet up in the air) and slid down to the floor. I turned it off and redid the start up procedure to get more practice controlling the drone. OH NO!!! all it does now is goes side ways and immediately lunges towards the floor. I can not believe how simple it is to destroy this plastic drone. I am a very cautious adult, thus buying this HS340 so that I would have experience under my belt before using a $150 dollar HS175D ( much better than the HS175) drone. I wanted to buy my HD175D from amazon but the D version was on e-xxx  dot com website for less money (after making an offer) and better camera plus better bearings. Now I see that the return window is closed so I will simply throw this $35 (sale price) dollar paper weight in the trash. Feleph Jungle Trees Building Blocks Bricks with 2 Base Plates (10 Inches for Each), Forest Garden Plants Flowers Bushes Animals Kit, Botanical Parts Scenery Toys Compatible with Major Brands LEGO would never make something like this. Sure, you can take their stuff and make anything with them, but too many of their kits make a definitive something. This is a definitive nothing, but a nothing that can entertain far beyond what a lot of different "somethings" can do.

LEGO is a toy, and this is often something that they remember to a fault. Here is a LEGO competitor, with bricks that are compatible, that remembers that it's not always a toy that kids want. They want an experience of playing, and that's what this Forest Garden kit gives them. Is it a dinosaur jungle? Is it a very nice tropical garden? Are the characters running from that alligator, or picnicing i the woods? With this, more than with any LEGO kit I've ever reviewed, there is a limitless number of possibilities.

There are no instructions with this kit, which is somewhat bothersome for the finnicky children who need a "right" way to put them together, but the playscape this provides is so unique that I can't give it less than 5 stars.

text_fidelity_a:
Magic The Gathering: Arena of the Planeswalkers Game This is a great value for what you're paying. Essentially, this game is based on another very good game called Heroscape. You'll build an arena out of the little pieces in this box, create an army, and do battle with one of the prepainted Planeswalker minis.

I picked this game up as a former MtG player. I was hugely involved in the game from Ice Age through Darksteel. I invested thousands of dollars in the game until it finally became apparent that I couldn't afford to continue to be competitive in the game. What I love about this is that there is a little of what I like about MtG - the deckbuilding, the spellcasting and the strategy - but not so much of what I don't like - the cost.

The game itself is solid if not spectacular. It accomodates up to 5 relatively seamlessly, and it's easy to set up the game as a 2 vs. 2 if you like the team approach, or to just make it a free-for-all. The biggest problem to me with the game, enough to lower it two full stars, is that the game feels like it is missing some essential element that will be added through expansions. It's difficult to identify exactly what it is, but I can't shake the feeling that they took something essential out and going to release it as a big box expansion in the next few months.

As it is, it's a solid game that feels unfinished. I'll eagerly look forward to the (I"m assuming) forthcoming expansion.
text_fidelity_b: Magic The Gathering: Arena of the Planeswalkers Game

Still the price was reasonable so I ordered one. This is not the first Klutz craft kit we've played with - so it was a familiar experience as those other kits. There really wasn't much in the box - the clay, a pencil (without an eraser), a sculpting tool, and a couple sheets of foldable paper props for the erasers you make (if you make the ones shown in the instructional guide).

You get plenty of different color clay - if you limit yourself to making fairly small erasers. The clay we got wasn't dried out - but it did take some kneeding to get soft enough to shape. Baking the erasers was simple - we used a toaster oven. Just be sure to use the right temperature and watch the erasers while they bake to make sure none start melting. Baking time can vary - mostly 15 to 30 minutes depending on the size & shape of the erasers you made.

The erasers are more ornamental than practical - but they do erase most pencil marks.

We're having fun with this kit - the instructional guide is outstanding. I'm happy with my purchase.

It was a good introduction to drone flying for me. I had planned on attaching a camera and expanding on my photography using this.

I will definitely need a bigger drone before I can do that but at least I was able to learn how to fly a drone since this is the first time I have ever had an experience with flying one.

What I enjoy about this is that it is easy to fly and the instruction manual was fairly easy to understand. It is small and lightweight so won't really injure somebody if it happens to crash land on somebody.

The drone itself has an extra set of blades in case the blades that are already on it get broken, as well as extra batteries for the drone itself. It even comes with a screw driver so you can open the battery compartments. This way no hunting down your own tools.

The remote used to fly the drone however requires some AAA batteries, which did not come with it but you can get those just about anywhere. The control looks much like a video game controller so kids and teens who are already adept with holding a video game pad will be able to master this in no time.

The drone performed well on its intitial flight for me, and I even got it to do a few flips and rolls as well.

This is a decent little starter drone.

text_fidelity_a:
Wild Republic Audubon Birds Canada Goose Plush with Authentic Bird Sound, Stuffed Animal, Bird Toys for Kids and Birders, 5 inches First thing I noticed was how close this stuffed goose resembled the real thing. Second, the sound effect was so realistic. And third, there was no way for the batteries to be removed. All three demands of mine has been met. Now I purchase a lot of duck and geese related items for the baby shower of my niece, my brother finally got a girl who though he was decent and good looking enough to reproduce with. So while I was confused on what Auntie of the year was going to give to my first born niece, I remembered all the years growing up where my brother tormented and made fun of. Then it dawned on me! I was going to gift all duck and geese related things to my niece so she will grow up loving them. Why you ask? Well I will share a story. Long ago, back in the mid 90’s my grandmother took my brother and I to the local duck pond to let us feed the ducks bread. I, obviously the intelligent one, knew to throw the bread as far away as I could away from me. My brother, a few fries short of a happy meal, threw it at his feet. Before he knew it all these mystical, beautiful beasts of the pond surrounded him. I remember him mocking me, “ you aren’t cool the ducks don’t like you”. And I can remember clearly him saying “ I AM THEIR GOD.” Then karma happened. All my Sunday school teaching happened as I sat in the car with my grandmother waiting for this false duck god to finish his loaf of bread it happened. Our almighty creater from above, the real God, spoke “There is no true God but me” and just like that my brother ran out of bed. These geese, realized he had no bread and he was a false prophet started to chant their battle cry! Next thing I knew, my brother started to get attacked by a mob of geese. Now he’s banging at my grandmother’s car door to let him in but she still laughing so hard she couldn’t reach over to unlock the door. (We didn’t have power doors during this time) I could of easily reached over and unlocked the door, but I sat back and watched this biblical lesson unfold in front of my eyes. Did you know geese have teeth on their tongue? He found out that day Eventually my grandma let him in and they surrounded the car for a good 10 minutes before they left to stalk their new prey.
That day I almost became an only child and that day changed my brother forever.

So yes this stuffed geese and all the other geese and duck related items from this seller is worth the money. It was amazing seeing a grown mad cowering in fear as he unwrapped every single duck and goose at his baby shower. His child is going to befriend the very creatures that almost murdered him in cold blood over a loaf of bread.
10/10 will buy from again.
text_fidelity_b: Wild Republic Audubon Birds Canada Goose Plush with Authentic Bird Sound, Stuffed Animal, Bird Toys for Kids and Birders, 5 inches

eeBoo French Flash Cards I had the great fortune of parents who made sure I learned three other languages as a kid. They started very early with me and I distinctly remember them making their own flashcards. It's too bad that they didn't have access to these beautiful, affordable, and very easy to use flashcards to aid them! Now, as a parent, teacher, and a nanny, I work hard to teach my kids the basics of French and Spanish, and I stumbled across these. They have been well worth the price and they were highly affordable. Best of all, my kids that I teach love the cards and enjoy using them too. I would recommend them to both the beginner and the advanced speaker as they embark on teaching others.

There are a few times that the cards use outdated pronunciations or word choices, but it's actually a plus in my book because it aids further in teaching. When I see a card with a different context of pronunciation or word choice than what is currently popular or commonly used, then I can supplement by saying "Or you could say it like this ..." Anyways, the cards are really lovely and sturdy. They seem sort of indestructible because one of the kids I nanny is 18 months old and a total "rip things to shreds" sort and he wasn't even able to destroy one! They also wipe off nicely with a damp cloth.

Do consider using these for your own kids! You wont be sorry!

Thames & Kosmos Wind Power V4.0 STEM Experiment Kit | Build a 3ft Wind Turbine to Generate Electricity | Learn About Renewable Energy & Power a Small Model Car | Weatherproof for Outdoor Use This kit was a lot more fun for Dad than it was for the kid. She's younger than the recommended age range, but had little trouble putting the whole model together in under 30 minutes with Dad's help. We barely used the book for assembly, but read the more educational "science" book cover to cover.

She and I talk all the time about renewable energy, largely because solar panels are looking like the next big home improvement project around here, and we get what I'd consider a reasonable amount of wind. She found the concepts easy enough to understand, and was interested to see what we'd be able to do in the backyard...and it's not much. The wind we got was not nearly enough to make this project effective, even on what I'd consider a relatively windy day. I put it on the roof for a short time and that helped, but not much. The turbine requires a battery, which makes both of us question where the small amount of power we are generating actually comes from.

So the experiments died off rather quickly, and this became a very short model building project for her that Dad is enjoying tinkering with to see if he can charge one of those rechargable cell-phone batteries. Kid is off playing with the very small toy car that comes with the kit, but doesn't look like it belongs at all.

If you get a lot of wind, then it's probably a lot more fun, but it's for the younger age of the spectrum for sure.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Wind Power V4.0 STEM Experiment Kit | Build a 3ft Wind Turbine to Generate Electricity | Learn About Renewable Energy & Power a Small Model Car | Weatherproof for Outdoor Use

When we opened up the package, we had a couple of issues with the wood being cracked.  The overall setup is fairly easy if you follow the directions.  Customer service was really great working with when I called to get replacement parts.  To be clear, though, I wasn't aware that we'd have to seal the playhouse.  I only found that out because I'd called for replacement parts.  We used a marine sealant and it is full waterproofing!  We used a chemical pump sprayer to apply it (we sprayed it on and then brushed over it - it is very runny like milk and goes on white but dries clear).  I, originally, expected the wood to be pre-sealed since it was a playhouse specifically for outside.  So, in hindsight, I am very grateful that we talked with the helpful customer service person.  Otherwise, we'd probably have to be replacing the house next year ... and, I wouldn't have been very happy with the purchase.  However, we've had it a couple months now and it still looks brand new!  I'd highly recommend this playhouse IF you are willing to seal it.  Yes, marine clear coat is expensive but so was the playhouse.  All in all, a great addition to our backyard and I'm sure we'll get several years of grandchildren's fun with it!

text_fidelity_a: Perplexus Rookie (Styles and Colors Vary) My 8 year old daughter received the Perplexus for Christmas, and our whole family fought over it for the rest of the holiday break. It's wonderful to see my very large, very rough and tumble four year old boy carefully, slowly, cautiously navigate this little ball bearing around the maze. He has beaten it, but that doesn't seem to diminish his interest in trying again.  Whoever came up with this idea for this toy has my respect.  I only gave it four stars for durability because it seems like it could be a little higher quality.  For such an amazing toy, the materials should be of a high enough quality to make it an heirloom.  It is honestly one of my favorite toys, along with quadrilla and magnatiles, so I wish it was a little more substantial. POKONBOY Rainbow Scratch Art Paper Kits for Kids, 50 PCS Magic Scratch Paper with 5 Wooden Styluses and 4 Stencils - Black Scratch Off Arts and Crafts Supplies Christmas Birthday Gift This is "scratch paper" in the most literal sense. Your children will use the included wooden stakes, or maybe even toothpicks, to score designs into the surface of a black piece of paper. As they scratch, the colors that make up the underlying layers start to show through, and create brilliant drawings.

It's a very nice little project for young ones that doesn't take too much time, or too much effort. Outside of a little sweeping to take care of the fine black bits that fall off the surface of the paper, there isn't much to this one. Of course, the nature of the product requires that your little artist will have to be careful, and take their time, as there's no erasing. I make mine plan out her drawing ahead of time, and make a practice copy before transferring the image to the final piece. Of course, there's always stencils, but those won't be for everyone.

The pages in this kit are nice and thick, but only about the size of two index cards put side-by-side. I was kind of hoping for something a little bigger. The scratch sticks are good quality, as are the stencils.

Overall, a great rainy-day project.

They have always been great quality and sturdy, usually made from wood and painted. This set of puzzles was disappointing to say the least. The pieces are thin instead of the usual "chunky" pieces I'm used to, and the colored parts of the pieces are just stickers that are glued on. text_fidelity_a:
Sesame Street Playskool Discover ABCs with Elmo Playset This toy is pretty neat.

There's not much as far as assembly goes. (Just snapping 3 pieces together, and then attaching the whole building into that.) It only took a minute or so.

Elmo is detached from the rest of the set, and he holds onto a hand "lens". Letters are hidden throughout the building, on both sides. You can tell where a letter is going to be...circle with squiggly lines. You can't tell what letter it is until Elmo's "lens" is held over it, though. To find some of the letters, the child will have to turn a couple of wheels, and lift the trash can lid, but most of them are in plain view.

This is a fun little toy for learning letters. It doesn't take up a ton of room, either. It's somewhat flat in design, so it could easily slide into a little nook somewhere, and just pull it out for learning time. I think most children will tire quickly of it if they have full access to it, unless they have other Sesame Street toys(or something else similar) that could be used with it, apart from just hunting for letters. I think it's probably better for special times, though, for most children. There's really not a great deal to it, but it is fun and neat.
text_fidelity_b: Sesame Street Playskool Discover ABCs with Elmo Playset

text_fidelity_a: Klutz Watercolor Dreams Craft Kit, 11 Piece Set, Multicolor I do think that the Klutz series of art kits are mainly targeted to kids, but I love them even as an adult. This watercolor set is no exception. It's convenient for a quick de-stressing art event, almost like a coloring book, except for painting. I don't have to gather tons of supplies or draw anything to paint. Other than getting some water and maybe a paper towel to go with it, I'm good to go. Within this set is a painting book, watercolors, and a paintbrush. The pages are thick(with the design on only one side) and I haven't had any issues with color/water running to the other pages, or even to the back of the one I'm working on. The pages do have a tear off feature, so they're easy to remove. The paintbrush isn't the nicest watercolor brush ever, but it is incredibly nice for what I'd expect in a kit like this. The same goes for the paints. It all works well for fun. There are tips in the beginning of the book for how to hold the brush for different needs. It takes some practice to get it to do okay for the detail work(which isn't super detailed), but it paints well. There's also advice on mixing for different colors. It's a fun book! I like pulling it out for when I need a little no-stress art.

text_fidelity_a: Air Hogs - Supernova, Gravity Defying Hand-Controlled Flying Orb, for Ages 8 and Up Still learning!!  This has had our house in a happy uproar since we got it!  After multiple readings of directions and many try outs we think we kind of have a handle on the basics but doing any tricks are an accidental result only.  Batteries are already in this.  Everything for power is concentrated in the center of this orb.  It comes w/USB to charge through our computer.  There is a tiny, tiny white slide tab in center by batteries that you move to turn this on.  Immediately (if charged) the center ball light will come on and flash colors.  When charging or a problem, the ball light will flash red only.  This is a fairly fragile  plastic caged flyer.  It doesn't weigh a lot because it has to keep it's self flying + hovering with 4 little sets of plastic blades that rotate (think fan blades).  Four extra blades come with this. Inside the orb besides the power center and the blades are sensors that will cause the orb to change directions when they are blocked in any way. To start, you have it on and slowly let it drop out of yr hands, it will drop and start hovering before it actually hits the floor(the sensors realize there is something in the way). After it starts hovering low over floor you get a hand(s) underneath and just start raising it and moving it all over the place by using yr hands to block the sensors...All the while, center light is flashing colors and the orb is making this noise..lol, between a whine & buzz and you find yrself almost running around the room trying to control this thing!  It will go up to the ceiling and then you have to figure out how to get a hand up to control it!  We don't dare take it outside to do, afraid it wouldn't come back!  This has fallen to the floor several times and not broken but, it is something you should take care with.  A lot of great accidental exercise and laughs!  Not for little children to use but they will love the show
text_fidelity_b: Air Hogs - Supernova, Gravity Defying Hand-Controlled Flying Orb, for Ages 8 and Up

Transformers Protectobot Action Figure (2-Pack) At first, I thought the age range on this toy was a bit too low. Then after my children gave these up and Dad got on the job, I realized quickly that the toys were just not that great.

Hot Spot is a fire truck with a really long crane on his hand that you're not supposed to be able to take off, making him awkward to pose as a robot. Once you get him into robot mode, which is no easy feat, you'll have a heck of a time getting him back into firetruck mode. Even once he's there, you can clearly see his robot hands on the top of the truck, and his legs (which form the bottom of the truck and include the back wheels), will consistently half-transform while trying to wheel him around on the ground.

All this and Hotspot is the better half of the duo. Blades, the helicopter, looks like an awkward chicken when transformed into robot mode, which is not helped by the fact that he appears to not have any hands or arms. The instructions for transforming him were incredibly difficult to decipher, as they have frequent close ups of pieces which I can't really find on my model and curvy arrows pointing at different spots. If a 31 year old with a master's degree can't figure him out, how do we expect a 6-year-old with limited patience to do it?
text_fidelity_b: Transformers Protectobot Action Figure (2-Pack)

text_fidelity_a:
Tenergy TB6-B Balance Charger Discharger 1S-6S Digital Battery Pack Charger for NiMH/NiCD/Li-PO/Li-Fe Packs LCD Hobby Battery Charger w/ Tamiya/JST/EC3/HiTec/Deans Connectors + Power Supply 01435 This unit comes with almost everything you need to --

-- charge your LiPo's rapidly
-- balance charge your LiPo's so each cell has the same voltage
-- discharge your LiPo's if they're fully charged but you want to store them
-- charge your LiPo's to storage voltage levels for long term storage
-- plug your charger into AC wall power

The adapter cable fits a large variety of cell terminal plugs.

There is a balance port that receives the included balance plug adapter that can connect to anything up to 8S batteries.

This particular kit comes with an AC power supply like those that come with computers. The charger is really designed to hook to a car battery or other 12VDC high amperage source. This AC supply lets you plug it in at home easily and reliably. It comes with the right plug to fit perfectly.

The only things that could be added are extension cables on the balance connector to make it easier to charge the cells by making all the wires about the same length. [[ASIN:B00JBP32A0 JST JST-XH 3S Balance Wire Extention 20cm adapter 11.1v LiPo Battery Cable Li-Po]] This also allows you to put the cells into a fireproof bag during charging. [[ASIN:B005Q3VSZC Bluecell Black Medium Size Lipo Battery Guard Sleeve/Bag for Charge & Storage]]

One other accessory that really helps is a compact voltage indicator [[ASIN:B003Y6E6IE Integy C23212 Lipo Voltage Checker/Warning Buzzer]] that you plug into the balance port on the battery. Not strictly needed for recharging, but is very useful to monitor voltage after charging.

You'll need to consult YouTube for useful instructions on how to manipulate the four buttons and why, unless you want to read the manual. And who reads manuals anymore when a good ten minute video is clearer and simpler?

text_fidelity_a:
Harrisville Designs Lap Loom Kit, Hand Weaving for Kids and Adults (Style B) I used to make wall hangings as a child with homemade looms. I recently met someone who weaves huge items and after seeing photos of her work my interest in weaving was renewed. I like the simplicity of these looms but do have some comments. Firstly, the frame is wood with plastic pegs. A screw in each corner holds the frame together but mine is a bit loose. I may need to tighten later. Instruction booklet is well written, read all the way through before starting because there are tips later on in the booklet. Parents please note that every other row you must insert a second flat shed stick into the loom. It's not complicated, just takes time so be aware if your child may not have patience to do this.
My only complaint is I ordered the bigger size B loom and in the photo on Amazon it showed yarn in orange, yellow and reds so I bought a refill yarn kit called Sierra because it was black and red and I thought it would be nice to have both but when my loom arrived I see the size B comes with the black and red yarn and the smaller sized A has the oranges. So now I'll have two black and red items :( I don't know where the photo came from but it should be corrected!
The manufacturers website shows the correct colors but I didn't go there until after I got my loom. I would also recommend spending $10 more to get the Wonderloom. It helps push the yarn down evenly.

Educational Insights Teacup Pile-Up! Relay Game, Preschool Board Game, Gift for Kids Ages 4+ This Tea Cup Pile Up game is so fun! I had a blast playing it with my kiddo. There were some tears at first when a few of the tea cup towers toppled over, and I had to explain that’s why the game is challenging and it’s about practicing how to balance everything. Once we got over that hurdle, and a few extra practice rounds, we both just loved it!

There’s enough components to build 2 towers per face-off challenge—each side includes 1 flat thick cardboard tray, 4 plates and 4 cups (all of that x2 for the whole game). The card shows the order in which the tower needs to built for each round, and the first person to build it without it falling over dings the tea pot bell as the winner. The tea pot bell isn’t very pronounced in its sound, which is a good thing that it’s not too loud, but a little underwhelming when you’re excited to ring the bell when you win! It's just a charming design for a stacking and pattern recognition game, and it's definitely fun! Five stars!

text_fidelity_a:
The Resistance I picked up The Resistance to play at family gatherings where mafia and werewolf didn't go over so well. People didn't like getting eliminated and didn't like someone needing to moderate/narrate the game. The resistance is best played with more people. The more the merrier definitely is true here. Some people will play as the resistance and some as spies. The spies are trying to sabotage the missions while the resistance is trying to complete the missions. The game has a mission leader who will pick which players are going to go on the mission. The game then opens discussion to all players to decide if that is the best choice of players for the mission.

Overall, We enjoyed the game, but when playing with only 5 players, it's a bit too easy and people don't really get into the discussion. When playing with 8-10 players, the game is a lot more fun as people really get into the accusations and deciding who should go on the different missions. Since people aren't eliminated like mafia and werewolf, people tend to enjoy this game more.
text_fidelity_b: The Resistance

text_fidelity_a:
Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb. Most reviews mention the mind-boggling size of the model; I figured that it was because when we gain fatty tissue, it's distributed in a thin layer over our bodies, so seeing it as a lump would be surprising to most people.

     Even with the warnings, I was still shocked! It looked like it had to be 8-10 pounds, not a mere 5! And it FELT like 6-8 pounds...

After a while, I got curious as to why it seemed so disproportionately large. I'm aware that I consistently make terrible (truly awful) estimations of volumes, distances, and weights, so I measured it, just to get the actual numbers.

     My kitchen scale gave the model's mass as 5.293 pounds. That's a forgivable degree of error: 6%. Definitely closer than my awful guesstimate of 6-8 pounds.

     I used displacement to measure the volume as 11.75 cups. [I filled a container to overflowing with water. I added the model to displace some water, then removed the model. I carefully measured how much water I added to completely refill the container.]

     Google conversions gives 11.75 cups as being 169.6 in^3. Various sites list the volume of a pound of adipose tissue as being 29 in^3, 29.5 in^3, 30.08 in^3, and 30.42 in^3.

Using the model's volume and the lowest density, I calculate the model's representative mass as:
169.6 in^3 ÷ 30.42 in^3/lbs = 5.577 lbs

And using the highest density to calculate my model's "mass":
169.6 in^3 ÷ 29 in^3/lbs = 5.8 lbs (17% greater than 5 pounds, but well under my 8-10 pound guess.)

So whether you are measuring by weight or volume, the model is 6-17% oversized. That's far more accurate than seemed possible.

Obviously the manufacturer had to compromise between approximating the coloration, texture, pliablity, volume, and weight. I'm not a surgeon, so I'm clueless as to the accuracy of the coloration, texture, and pliablity. I am disappointed that the volume (which was the characteristic I was most interested in) was off by more than 5%.
text_fidelity_b: Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb.

text_fidelity_a: Monterey LG8510 Lady Bug Lure, Pack of 3 I buy these lures each year ever since I learned that ladybugs like to cluster in small hollow space in houses. One year I had 1 exterior wall with over 1000 ladybugs crawling on it in the sunshine, a day later they were all gone and over the following weeks they started falling out of the cracks inside my house. Every morning as soon as the sun rose I would start finding them everywhere. I checked the internet and found the Ladybuglady who told me that ladybugs cluster in the late fall to stay warm through the winter. If they find a space like a house and a way in they will literally take over the sun side wall of the house. The way to avoid this was to build ladybug houses (similar to bird house but with smaller holes) and place them in your garden and orchards where the Ladybugs will benefit your plants (they eat aphids) and get these lures to draw them to the houses. Well for 2 years it has worked like a charm. No ladybugs in my houses and the trees in my orchard are doing very well.
text_fidelity_b: Monterey LG8510 Lady Bug Lure, Pack of 3

text_fidelity_a:
Cosco Funsport Deluxe Play Yard, Monster Syd One day I'm gonna miss the fum little prisons that keep our little one out of harms way, but until that day, I love this little crate for children.

It's nothing revolutionary--hell, after my St Bernard grew tired of his crate I thought--damn, this would be great for children. Apparently someone else thought that, and from the likes of what's out there, a few others did as well. Anyway, we've evolved to the point where decorative monsters and fun colors make it seem more humane and fun and less "now I have my hands free to drink a beer" (note that I do not use this to support my drinking habits, as I'm ok with kids crawling on the dirt while I drink--I just hate doing added laundry). The monsters seem to amuse me more than junior, but perhaps that says something about the dark voices I hear rather than the artistic merits of the designers. I appreciate them nonetheless. The collapsing and folding bit is nice, so we can take it to family day at the demolition derby or one of those bikini car washes. The "sets up in under 1 minute" is true, but it's even quicker if you do it yourself (junior is still working on the hand-eye coordination) and you put down the beer. Best of all--the wheels! Why fold it up and take up all the space in your car for a car seat, when you can tie this to the back of the family truckster and give junior a chance to enjoy the great outdoors while you drive! The comprehensive padding (and bouncy floor) will come in handy when junior joins the toddler wrestling set, and future WWE fortunes will easily cover the modest investment in this play yard.

In all honestly, this is a nice play set. No kids gets were harmed, neglected, or otherwise in need of CPS. Have a great day.
text_fidelity_b: Cosco Funsport Deluxe Play Yard, Monster Syd

text_fidelity_a: Libay Jigsaw Puzzle Mat Roll Up, Puzzle Saver Store 500 1000 1500 2000 Pieces Felt Puzzle Mat with 9 Pieces Puzzle Glue Sheets for Kids and Adults, Hand Pump Inflatable Tube and Storage Bag 42" X 29" I really wish I had got one of these years ago. It would’ve saved so many pieces from disappearing and the headache of finally finishing a puzzle only to be short a piece or two. This mat is perfect for both a puzzle workspace and keeping it together when you need to put it up for a bit. The first puzzle I did on this mat was circular and I found the printed outlines to be very useful in knowing how big the puzzle was going to be. It has several circular and rectangular sizes preprinted, which would work for the majority of puzzles. The material is great for keeping your pieces in place since it’s slightly fuzzy. The mat rolls up perfectly around the inflatable tube and the Velcro straps keep it all together. One piece of advice: don’t leave any loose pieces too close to the edge because they will fall out when you unroll the mat. The bag is great too so you can keep the felt from getting dusty and it makes it easy to carry. I’m very happy to have this mat. Now I can actually start doing puzzles again without having to leave it out to the mercy of my toddler and my cats. Great product!
text_fidelity_b: Libay Jigsaw Puzzle Mat Roll Up, Puzzle Saver Store 500 1000 1500 2000 Pieces Felt Puzzle Mat with 9 Pieces Puzzle Glue Sheets for Kids and Adults, Hand Pump Inflatable Tube and Storage Bag 42" X 29"
